components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one main action on a screen, with its shortcut keycap.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 9px; padding: 10px 16px; font: 600 14px 'Funnel Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; background: oklch(46% 0.115 248); color: oklch(98% 0.005 250); transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background-color 120ms ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(50% 0.12 248); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(54% 0.14 255); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-key { font: 500 11px/1 'Funnel Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; border-radius: 4px; padding: 3px 5px; background: oklch(98% 0.005 250 / 0.16); }

components.name: Wire
components.description: Progress as conductors: solid mastered, striped learning, hollow not started.
components.css: .ds-wire { --c: oklch(60% 0.14 148); display: flex; gap: 3px; height: 10px; width: 220px; } .ds-wire i { flex: 1; border-radius: 2px; } .ds-wire i:first-child { border-radius: 5px 2px 2px 5px; } .ds-wire i:last-child { border-radius: 2px 5px 5px 2px; } .ds-solid { background: var(--c); } .ds-learn { background: linear-gradient(180deg, oklch(98.5% 0.003 250) 0 30%, var(--c) 30% 70%, oklch(98.5% 0.003 250) 70%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--c) 55%, transparent); } .ds-hollow { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.25px oklch(83% 0.012 250); }

components.name: Rail Nav Item
components.css: .ds-rail { background: oklch(46% 0.115 248); padding: 12px; display: grid; gap: 2px; width: 200px; } .ds-nav { border: 0; background: transparent; color: oklch(88% 0.03 248); padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 8px; text-align: left; font: 500 14px 'Funnel Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-nav:hover { background: oklch(98% 0.004 250 / 0.08); color: oklch(96% 0.01 250); } .ds-nav[aria-current='page'] { background: oklch(53% 0.12 248); color: oklch(96% 0.01 250); } .ds-nav:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(96% 0.01 250); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Octet takes one thing from networking and uses it everywhere: the colour code on the eight conductors inside every Ethernet cable. Course progress, network links, session steps and failed checks are all drawn as wires. Everything else is a quiet, standard desktop app.
keyCharacteristics: Progress drawn as wires: solid means mastered, white with a coloured stripe means learning or fading, hollow means not started.
The four T568B pairs name the four tracks: orange for CCNA 1, green for CCNA 2, blue for CCNA 3, brown for Beyond.
One signature interaction: click a cable to strip its jacket and see the VLAN conductors inside. A failed check shows as a cut conductor that closes when fixed.
No label ever sits above a title.

rules.name: The One Material Rule
rules.body: Jacket blue is one material. The rail, the primary button, the session cord and every drawn cable jacket use the same blue, never a near-miss.

rules.name: The Pair Rule
rules.body: A pair colour always means its course. Orange is never used to mean warning, and green only means a pass because CCNA 2 owns green in the lab where it appears.

rules.name: The Cut Rule
rules.body: Red appears only where something is broken, and it disappears the moment the fix lands.

rules.name: The Device Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is the voice of a device. Configs, ports, addresses and console output are mono. Keycaps, module numbers, counts and UI labels never are.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No label sits above a title. Dates go in the title bar, context goes in a line under the title, and step progress goes in the footer.

rules.name: The No Halo Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows. State is drawn with a ring, a fill or a wire, never a zero-offset coloured glow.
